# Gröbner bases for tropical polynomial semimodules

This file uses Mathlib's `Tropical`, `MvPolynomial`, `Submodule`, and
`MonomialOrder` rather than introducing replacement algebraic structures.
A tropical ideal is represented by the existing `Submodule` of the tropical
polynomial semiring.  We develop leading monomials, initial divisibility,
finite test-set Gröbner bases, and a finite Buchberger completion process.

The finite test set is explicit.  This is the setting in which the completion
algorithm is executable without assuming that arbitrary ideal membership is
decidable.  The termination theorem gives the usual finite Buchberger
conclusion: after at most the size of the test set, no unresolved leading
monomial remains.
-/

noncomputable section

open scoped MonomialOrder

namespace TropicalGroebner

variable {K σ : Type*} [CommSemiring K]

/-- Polynomials in the variables `σ` over `K`. -/
abbrev Polynomial (K σ : Type*) [CommSemiring K] := MvPolynomial σ K

/-- A tropical ideal is a tropical-linear subsemimodule of the polynomial
semiring.  This is an abbreviation for Mathlib's existing `Submodule`. -/
abbrev TropicalIdeal (K σ : Type*) [CommSemiring K] :=
  Submodule K (Polynomial K σ)

/-- The tropical ideal generated by a set of polynomials. -/
def generatedIdeal (S : Set (Polynomial K σ)) : TropicalIdeal K σ :=
  Submodule.span K S

/-- A support exponent is leading when it is maximal for the chosen monomial
order.  This relational presentation avoids choosing a leading coefficient. -/
def IsLeadingExponent (m : MonomialOrder σ) (p : Polynomial K σ)
    (e : σ →₀ ℕ) : Prop :=
  e ∈ p.support ∧ ∀ d ∈ p.support, d ≼[m] e

/-- Monomial divisibility, expressed componentwise on exponent vectors. -/
def MonomialDivides (a b : σ →₀ ℕ) : Prop := a ≤ b

/-- A polynomial is leading-reducible by a finite family when the leading
monomial of a family member divides its leading monomial. -/
def LeadingReducible (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)) (p : Polynomial K σ) : Prop :=
  ∃ g ∈ G, ∃ eg ep,
    IsLeadingExponent m g eg ∧ IsLeadingExponent m p ep ∧ MonomialDivides eg ep

/-- Gröbner basis relative to a finite test set `U`.  Every nonzero member of
`I ∩ U` has initial monomial divisible by one coming from `G`; all basis
members themselves belong to `I ∩ U`. -/
def IsGroebnerBasisOn [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) (U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)) : Prop :=
  G ⊆ U ∧ (∀ g ∈ G, g ∈ I) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ U, p ∈ I → p ≠ 0 → LeadingReducible m G p

/-- An obstruction is a nonzero tested ideal element whose leading monomial is
not yet reducible. -/
def IsObstruction [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) (U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ))
    (p : Polynomial K σ) : Prop :=
  p ∈ U ∧ p ∈ I ∧ p ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ LeadingReducible m G p

/-- The deterministic completion step adds one unresolved polynomial, chosen
from the finite test set, and does nothing when no obstruction remains. -/
noncomputable def buchbergerStep [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) (U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)) :
    Finset (Polynomial K σ) := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ p, IsObstruction m I U G p then insert (Classical.choose h) G else G

/-- Iterate the tropical Buchberger completion step. -/
def buchbergerIterate [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) (U : Finset (Polynomial K σ)) :
    ℕ → Finset (Polynomial K σ) → Finset (Polynomial K σ)
  | 0, G => G
  | n + 1, G => buchbergerIterate m I U n (buchbergerStep m I U G)

/-- A nonzero polynomial has a leading exponent for every monomial order. -/
theorem exists_isLeadingExponent [DecidableEq K] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    {p : Polynomial K σ} (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    ∃ e, IsLeadingExponent m p e := by
  obtain ⟨e, he, hmax⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_max_image p.support m.toSyn (MvPolynomial.support_nonempty.mpr hp)
  exact ⟨e, he, fun d hd => hmax d hd⟩

/-- Tropical ideals are closed under tropical addition. -/
theorem TropicalIdeal.add_mem {I : TropicalIdeal K σ} {p q : Polynomial K σ}
    (hp : p ∈ I) (hq : q ∈ I) : p + q ∈ I := by
  exact Submodule.add_mem I hp hq

/-- Tropical ideals are closed under tropical scalar multiplication. -/
theorem TropicalIdeal.smul_mem {I : TropicalIdeal K σ} (a : K)
    {p : Polynomial K σ} (hp : p ∈ I) : a • p ∈ I := by
  apply Submodule.smul_mem I a; exact hp

/-- The generated tropical ideal is the least tropical ideal containing its
specified generators. -/
theorem generatedIdeal_le_iff {S : Set (Polynomial K σ)} {I : TropicalIdeal K σ} :
    generatedIdeal S ≤ I ↔ S ⊆ I := by
  exact Submodule.span_le

/-- Every nonzero basis polynomial leading-reduces itself. -/
theorem leadingReducible_self [DecidableEq K] [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)]
    (m : MonomialOrder σ) {G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)} {p : Polynomial K σ}
    (hpG : p ∈ G) (hp : p ≠ 0) : LeadingReducible m G p := by
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := exists_isLeadingExponent m hp
  exact ⟨p, hpG, e, e, he, he, le_refl e⟩

/-- The Gröbner condition is exactly absence of an unresolved obstruction,
provided the proposed basis already lies in the tested part of the ideal. -/
theorem isGroebnerBasisOn_iff_no_obstruction [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)]
    (m : MonomialOrder σ) (I : TropicalIdeal K σ)
    {U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)} (hGU : G ⊆ U)
    (hGI : ∀ g ∈ G, g ∈ I) :
    IsGroebnerBasisOn m I U G ↔ ¬ ∃ p, IsObstruction m I U G p := by
  constructor
  · intro ⟨_, _, hGB⟩ h
    rcases h with ⟨p, hpU, hpI, hpne, hpnot⟩
    exact hpnot (hGB p hpU hpI hpne)
  · intro h
    exact ⟨hGU, hGI, fun p hpU hpI hpne => by
      by_contra hpnot
      exact h ⟨p, hpU, hpI, hpne, hpnot⟩⟩

/-- A completion step never removes a polynomial. -/
theorem subset_buchbergerStep [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)]
    (m : MonomialOrder σ) (I : TropicalIdeal K σ)
    (U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)) :
    G ⊆ buchbergerStep m I U G := by
  unfold buchbergerStep
  split_ifs with h
  · exact Finset.subset_insert _ _
  · exact Finset.Subset.refl _

/-- If the current family lies in the finite universe, so does the result of a
completion step. -/
theorem buchbergerStep_subset_universe [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)]
    (m : MonomialOrder σ) (I : TropicalIdeal K σ)
    {U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)} (hGU : G ⊆ U) :
    buchbergerStep m I U G ⊆ U := by
  unfold buchbergerStep
  split_ifs with h
  · rw [Finset.insert_subset_iff]
    exact ⟨(Classical.choose_spec h).1, hGU⟩
  · exact hGU

/-- Completion preserves membership of every basis polynomial in the ideal. -/
theorem buchbergerStep_mem_ideal [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)]
    (m : MonomialOrder σ) (I : TropicalIdeal K σ)
    {U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)} (hGI : ∀ g ∈ G, g ∈ I) :
    ∀ g ∈ buchbergerStep m I U G, g ∈ I := by
  unfold buchbergerStep
  split_ifs with h
  · intro g hg
    rw [Finset.mem_insert] at hg
    rcases hg with rfl | hg
    · exact (Classical.choose_spec h).2.1
    · exact hGI g hg
  · exact hGI

/-- If an obstruction exists, one completion step strictly enlarges the
current family. -/
theorem card_lt_card_buchbergerStep_of_obstruction
    [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) {U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)}
    (hobs : ∃ p, IsObstruction m I U G p) :
    G.card < (buchbergerStep m I U G).card := by
  haveI : DecidableEq K := Classical.decEq K
  unfold buchbergerStep
  have hchoose := Classical.choose_spec hobs
  simp only [hobs, ↓reduceDIte]
  have hnotin : Classical.choose hobs ∉ G := by
    intro h
    apply hchoose.2.2.2
    exact leadingReducible_self m h hchoose.2.2.1
  have hinsert : G ⊂ insert (Classical.choose hobs) G := by
    refine Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.mpr ⟨Finset.subset_insert _ G, ?_⟩
    intro heq
    have hcard : G.card = (insert (Classical.choose hobs) G).card := heq ▸ rfl
    rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hnotin] at hcard
    omega
  exact Finset.card_lt_card hinsert

/-- **Finite tropical Buchberger theorem.**  Starting from tested ideal
members, repeated completion reaches a Gröbner basis on `U` after at most
`U.card` steps. -/
theorem exists_buchberger_completion [DecidableEq K]
    [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) (U G₀ : Finset (Polynomial K σ))
    (hG₀U : G₀ ⊆ U) (hG₀I : ∀ g ∈ G₀, g ∈ I) :
    ∃ n ≤ U.card,
      IsGroebnerBasisOn m I U (buchbergerIterate m I U n G₀) := by
  -- First establish that each iterate stays within U
  have hIter_subset : ∀ n G, G ⊆ U → buchbergerIterate m I U n G ⊆ U := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero => simp [buchbergerIterate]
    | succ n ih =>
      intro G hGU
      simp [buchbergerIterate]
      exact ih _ (buchbergerStep_subset_universe m I hGU)
  -- Also establish that each iterate stays within I
  have hIter_mem : ∀ n G, (∀ g ∈ G, g ∈ I) → ∀ g ∈ buchbergerIterate m I U n G, g ∈ I := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero => simp [buchbergerIterate]
    | succ n ih =>
      intro G hGI g hg
      simp [buchbergerIterate] at hg
      exact ih _ (buchbergerStep_mem_ideal m I hGI) _ hg
  -- Use contradiction: if no Gröbner basis within U.card steps, cardinalities strictly increase
  by_contra h_no_basis
  push_neg at h_no_basis
  set Gn := fun n => buchbergerIterate m I U n G₀ with hGn_def
  -- Key: buchbergerIterate n G = buchbergerStep applied n times
  have hIterStep : ∀ n G, buchbergerIterate m I U (n + 1) G = buchbergerIterate m I U n (buchbergerStep m I U G) := by
    intro n G; rfl
  -- buchbergerIterate n G = buchbergerStep applied n times to G
  have hIter_n_time : ∀ n G, buchbergerIterate m I U n G = (fun G => buchbergerStep m I U G)^[n] G := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero => simp [buchbergerIterate]
    | succ n ih =>
      intro G
      rw [buchbergerIterate, ih]
      -- Need: f^[n] (f G) = f (f^[n] G)
      induction n with
      | zero => simp
      | succ n _ => simp [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
  have hGn_succ : ∀ n, Gn (n + 1) = buchbergerStep m I U (Gn n) := by
    intro n
    simp only [hGn_def]
    rw [hIter_n_time, hIter_n_time]
    exact Function.iterate_succ_apply' _ _ _
  -- Each Gn ⊆ U and elements in I
  have hGn_subset : ∀ n, Gn n ⊆ U := fun n => hIter_subset n G₀ hG₀U
  have hGn_mem : ∀ n, ∀ g ∈ Gn n, g ∈ I := fun n => hIter_mem n G₀ hG₀I
  -- If Gn is not a Gröbner basis, then card(Gn+1) > card(Gn)
  have hCardLT : ∀ n, ¬ IsGroebnerBasisOn m I U (Gn n) → (Gn n).card < (Gn (n + 1)).card := by
    intro n hn
    rw [hGn_succ]
    apply card_lt_card_buchbergerStep_of_obstruction m I
    rw [isGroebnerBasisOn_iff_no_obstruction m I (hGn_subset n) (fun g hg => hGn_mem n g hg)] at hn
    exact not_not.mp hn
  -- Now derive contradiction: cardinalities strictly increasing but bounded
  -- For each n ≤ U.card, Gn n is not a Gröbner basis, so card(Gn(n+1)) > card(Gn n)
  have hCardLT_le : ∀ n ≤ U.card, (Gn n).card < (Gn (n + 1)).card := by
    intro n hn
    exact hCardLT n (h_no_basis n hn)
  -- card(Gn n) ≥ n for all n ≤ U.card + 1
  have hCardGE : ∀ n ≤ U.card + 1, n ≤ (Gn n).card := by
    intro n hn
    induction n with
    | zero => exact Nat.zero_le _
    | succ n ih =>
      have hn' : n ≤ U.card := Nat.le_of_succ_le_succ hn
      exact Nat.succ_le_of_lt (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (ih (hn'.trans (Nat.le_succ _))) (hCardLT_le n hn'))
  -- But also card(Gn n) ≤ U.card
  have hCardLE : ∀ n, (Gn n).card ≤ U.card := fun n => Finset.card_le_card (hGn_subset n)
  -- So U.card + 1 ≤ (Gn (U.card + 1)).card ≤ U.card, contradiction
  specialize hCardGE (U.card + 1) (le_refl _)
  have h := hCardLE (U.card + 1)
  omega

/-- A completed family is a fixed point of the Buchberger step. -/
theorem buchbergerStep_eq_self_of_groebner
    [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) {U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)}
    (hG : IsGroebnerBasisOn m I U G) :
    buchbergerStep m I U G = G := by
  unfold buchbergerStep
  have hno : ¬ ∃ p, IsObstruction m I U G p :=
    (isGroebnerBasisOn_iff_no_obstruction m I hG.1 hG.2.1).mp hG
  rw [dif_neg hno]

valid tested ideal members.  This is the algorithmic characterization of
finite tropical Gröbner bases. -/
theorem isGroebnerBasisOn_iff_buchberger_fixedPoint
    [DecidableEq (Polynomial K σ)] (m : MonomialOrder σ)
    (I : TropicalIdeal K σ) {U G : Finset (Polynomial K σ)}
    (hGU : G ⊆ U) (hGI : ∀ g ∈ G, g ∈ I) :
    IsGroebnerBasisOn m I U G ↔ buchbergerStep m I U G = G := by
  constructor
  · intro hGroebner
    apply buchbergerStep_eq_self_of_groebner m I hGroebner
  · intro hFixed
    unfold IsGroebnerBasisOn
    refine ⟨hGU, hGI, ?_⟩
    intro p hpU hpI hp0
    by_contra hNotReducible
    rw [buchbergerStep] at hFixed
    have hObs : IsObstruction m I U G p := ⟨hpU, hpI, hp0, hNotReducible⟩
    split at hFixed <;> simp_all

    -- The chosen element is an obstruction but in G, so it should be self-reducible
    have hq := Classical.choose_spec (by tauto : ∃ p, IsObstruction m I U G p)

    -- hq.2.2.2 : ¬LeadingReducible m G (Classical.choose h✝)

    have he := Classical.choose_spec hEx

    refine ⟨e, e, he, he, ?_⟩

# Exponential bounds for diagonal Ramsey numbers: the analytic interface

This file isolates the final quantitative step used by sub-four diagonal Ramsey
bounds.  The combinatorial part of such an argument typically produces a fixed
multiplicative saving `q < 1` per clique size, giving a bound `(4q)^k`.  The
results below convert that estimate, without asymptotic notation, into the
standard form `(4 - ε)^k` with one fixed `ε > 0`.

sequence: it makes no new graph or Ramsey-number definition.  Consequently the
lemmas can be applied directly to any existing encoding of diagonal Ramsey
numbers.

namespace RamseyBounds

/-- A sequence has an eventual diagonal-Ramsey-style upper bound with base
strictly below four. -/
def HasSubFourUpperBound (r : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 4 ∧ ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, (r k : ℝ) ≤ (4 - ε) ^ k

/-- A fixed proportional saving over the classical base four. -/
def HasProportionalSaving (r : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ q : ℝ, 0 < q ∧ q < 1 ∧ ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, (r k : ℝ) ≤ (4 * q) ^ k

/-- The exact change of variables between a proportional saving `q` and an
additive saving `ε`. -/
theorem four_mul_eq_four_sub_saving {q : ℝ} :
    4 * q = 4 - 4 * (1 - q) := by
  ring

This is the final algebraic passage from a bound of the shape `(4q)^k` to the
usual `(4-ε)^k` formulation. -/
theorem hasSubFourUpperBound_of_proportionalSaving {r : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : HasProportionalSaving r) : HasSubFourUpperBound r := by
  obtain ⟨q, hq_pos, hq_lt_one, k₀, hk₀⟩ := h
  use 4 * (1 - q)
  refine ⟨by linarith, by linarith, k₀, ?_⟩
  intro k hk
  have := hk₀ k hk
  rwa [four_mul_eq_four_sub_saving] at this

normalized as `(4q)^k` for a fixed `q ∈ (0,1)`. -/

    (h : HasSubFourUpperBound r) : HasProportionalSaving r := by
  obtain ⟨ε, hε_pos, hε_lt_4, k₀, hr⟩ := h
  use (4 - ε) / 4
  refine ⟨by linarith, by linarith, k₀, ?_⟩
  intro k hk
  have heq : (4 - ε : ℝ) = 4 * ((4 - ε) / 4) := by ring
  rw [heq] at hr
  exact hr k hk

theorem subFour_iff_proportionalSaving (r : ℕ → ℕ) :
    HasSubFourUpperBound r ↔ HasProportionalSaving r :=
  ⟨hasProportionalSaving_of_hasSubFourUpperBound,
    hasSubFourUpperBound_of_proportionalSaving⟩

sub-four gap `ε = 4(1-exp(-δ))`. -/

    HasSubFourUpperBound r := by

  -- Show ε > 0: since δ > 0, exp(-δ) < 1, so 1 - exp(-δ) > 0
  have hexp_lt_one : Real.exp (-δ) < 1 := by
    rw [Real.exp_lt_one_iff]
    exact neg_neg_of_pos hδ
  have hε_pos : 0 < 4 * (1 - Real.exp (-δ)) := by linarith
  refine ⟨hε_pos, ?_, ?_⟩
  -- Show ε < 4: since exp(-δ) > 0, we have 1 - exp(-δ) < 1, so 4*(1 - exp(-δ)) < 4
  have hexp_pos : 0 < Real.exp (-δ) := Real.exp_pos _
  linarith
  -- Need to convert (4 * exp(-δ))^k to (4 - 4*(1 - exp(-δ)))^k
  obtain ⟨k₀, hk₀⟩ := h
  exact ⟨k₀, fun k hk => by
    have : (4 : ℝ) * Real.exp (-δ) = 4 - 4 * (1 - Real.exp (-δ)) := by ring
    rw [← this]
    exact hk₀ k hk⟩

constant without losing the exponential improvement. -/

    (hq : 0 < q) (hqq' : q ≤ q')
    (h : ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, (r k : ℝ) ≤ (4 * q) ^ k) :
    ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, (r k : ℝ) ≤ (4 * q') ^ k := by
  obtain ⟨k₀, hk⟩ := h
  use k₀
  intro k hk'
  exact le_trans (hk k hk') (by gcongr)

    {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q) (hq_lt_one : q < 1)
    (h : ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀,
      (r k : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ d * (4 * q) ^ k) :
    HasSubFourUpperBound r := by
  let q' : ℝ := (q + 1) / 2
  have hq'_pos : 0 < q' := by
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hq'_lt_one : q' < 1 := by
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hbase : ‖(4 * q : ℝ)‖ < 4 * q' := by
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (mul_pos (by norm_num) hq)]
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hasym :=
    isLittleO_pow_const_mul_const_pow_const_pow_of_norm_lt d hbase
  have hev : ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      ‖(k : ℝ) ^ d * (4 * q) ^ k‖ ≤ 1 * ‖(4 * q') ^ k‖ :=
    hasym.bound zero_lt_one
  rw [Filter.eventually_atTop] at hev
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := hev
  obtain ⟨k₀, hk₀⟩ := h
  use 4 * (1 - q')
  refine ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith, max N k₀, ?_⟩
  intro k hk
  have hkN : N ≤ k := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hk
  have hkk₀ : k₀ ≤ k := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hk
  calc
    (r k : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ d * (4 * q) ^ k := hk₀ k hkk₀
    _ ≤ (4 * q') ^ k := by
      have hb := hN k hkN

        abs_of_nonneg

    exact neg_neg_of_pos hδ
  have hε_pos : 0 < 4 * (1 - Real.exp (-δ)) := by linarith
  refine ⟨hε_pos, ?_, ?_⟩
  -- Show ε < 4: since exp(-δ) > 0, we have 1 - exp(-δ) < 1, so 4*(1 - exp(-δ)) < 4
  have hexp_pos : 0 < Real.exp (-δ) := Real.exp_pos _
  linarith
  -- Need to convert (4 * exp(-δ))^k to (4 - 4*(1 - exp(-δ)))^k
  obtain ⟨k₀, hk₀⟩ := h
  exact ⟨k₀, fun k hk => by
    have : (4 : ℝ) * Real.exp (-δ) = 4 - 4 * (1 - Real.exp (-δ)) := by ring
    rw [← this]
    exact hk₀ k hk⟩

/-- A pointwise multiplicative saving is stable under replacing the saving
factor by a larger one.  This permits estimates to be rounded up to a simpler
constant without losing the exponential improvement. -/
theorem proportionalSaving_mono {r : ℕ → ℕ} {q q' : ℝ}
    (hq : 0 < q) (hqq' : q ≤ q')
    (h : ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, (r k : ℝ) ≤ (4 * q) ^ k) :
    ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, (r k : ℝ) ≤ (4 * q') ^ k := by
  obtain ⟨k₀, hk⟩ := h
  use k₀
  intro k hk'
  exact le_trans (hk k hk') (by gcongr)

/-- A fixed polynomial loss does not destroy a strict exponential saving.

More precisely, if `r k` is eventually at most `k^d (4q)^k` for one fixed
`q ∈ (0,1)`, then it is eventually bounded by `(4-ε)^k` for a fixed positive
`ε`.  The proof absorbs the polynomial into the larger saving factor
`q' = (q+1)/2`, which is still strictly below one. -/
theorem hasSubFourUpperBound_of_polynomialLoss {r : ℕ → ℕ} (d : ℕ)
    {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q) (hq_lt_one : q < 1)
    (h : ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀,
      (r k : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ d * (4 * q) ^ k) :
    HasSubFourUpperBound r := by
  let q' : ℝ := (q + 1) / 2
  have hq'_pos : 0 < q' := by
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hq'_lt_one : q' < 1 := by
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hbase : ‖(4 * q : ℝ)‖ < 4 * q' := by
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (mul_pos (by norm_num) hq)]
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hasym :=
    isLittleO_pow_const_mul_const_pow_const_pow_of_norm_lt d hbase
  have hev : ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      ‖(k : ℝ) ^ d * (4 * q) ^ k‖ ≤ 1 * ‖(4 * q') ^ k‖ :=
    hasym.bound zero_lt_one
  rw [Filter.eventually_atTop] at hev
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := hev
  obtain ⟨k₀, hk₀⟩ := h
  use 4 * (1 - q')
  refine ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith, max N k₀, ?_⟩
  intro k hk
  have hkN : N ≤ k := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hk
  have hkk₀ : k₀ ≤ k := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hk
  calc
    (r k : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ d * (4 * q) ^ k := hk₀ k hkk₀
    _ ≤ (4 * q') ^ k := by
      have hb := hN k hkN
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, one_mul,
        abs_of_nonneg (mul_nonneg (pow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) _)
          (pow_nonneg (le_of_lt (mul_pos (by norm_num) hq)) _)),
        abs_of_nonneg
          (pow_nonneg (le_of_lt (mul_pos (by norm_num) hq'_pos)) _)] at hb
      exact hb
    _ = (4 - 4 * (1 - q')) ^ k := by ring_nf

end RamseyBounds
